title: GPT-HateCheck: Can LLMs Write Better Functional Tests for Hate Speech Detection?
measurement_description: The paper measures hate speech targeting specific groups, one of which is Muslims. It evaluates the ability of Large Language Models to generate realistic and diverse hateful statements for this and other groups, and the ability of hate speech detection models to correctly classify them.
findings: The paper includes Muslims as one of seven protected target groups for generating hate speech test cases. The proposed framework, GPT-HATECHECK, was able to generate more diverse and natural-sounding hateful examples targeting Muslims compared to the original template-based HATECHECK dataset. For instance, an example of a filtered-out test case for Muslims was provided, where the model incorrectly identified 'Islam' as a homonymous slur. However, the paper does not offer specific findings or performance analyses for the Muslim group that are distinct from the other targeted groups.
